•Double-edged PD-1 arm mediating delivery of the IL-12 cytokine to tumor antigen-experienced CD8+ and CD4+ T cells while releasing the brakes through PD-1/PD-L1 pathway blockade
•pH-dependent CD25 mAb allowing binding to target cells only in the acidic TME, avoiding on-target off-tumor toxicities

•T cells-infiltrated solid tumors (hot and cold), immunotherapy-resistant
•Specific indications will be selected according to transcriptomic (scRNAseq), proteomics, and IHC/IF data analysis
•FIC by novel mode of action (MoA) and targets association within a bispecific agent
FiC
•Relapse-refractory solid tumors (hot and cold)

•IV as fastest path to reach clinical PoC; depending on the safety profile, SC administration may be considered
•Scheduling TBD (ideally Q2W)

•Improved OS/PFS versus standard-of-care treatments
•Clinical benefit as single agent with deep and durable anti-tumor responses 
•Potential synergy with approved ICP, vaccine, ACT, immune cell engagers or radio/chemotherapy
•Aim at reducing off-tumor toxicity observed in the clinics with rhIL-12 and by increasing tumor retention via PD-1, CD25 (pH-dependent), or ICOS

TCP_CHARACTERISTIC: Aspiration Goal (executive summary in one sentence)
TCP_CHARACTERISTIC_VALUE: •To develop a central nervous system-penetrant type I interferon receptor antagonist to block the propagation of neurodegeneration.

•Type I interferon signaling is mediated by a heterodimeric receptor composed of IFNAR1 and IFNAR2. Here, a bispecific antibody consisting of one arm targeting IFNAR1 to block type-I IFN signaling and the other arm featuring anti-TFRC to enhance CNS exposure. Since interferon is secreted by neurons as well as glia, Sanofi’s bispecific antibody will prevent the propagation of signaling across neural circuits.
•Alzheimer’s disease (AD) & Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)
FiC

•Confirmed diagnosis of MCI-AD (Mild Cognitive Impairment due to AD) or mild AD (CDR:0.5-1 with confirmed amyloid pathology)

•Confirmed diagnosis of ALS

•TE/POM: post-hoc analysis of IFN pathway biomarkers towards patient stratification strategy; Disease: pTau217, Aβ42/Aβ40, GFAP, NfL, neurogranin, SNAP-25
•IV or SC. FIH IV as fastest path to reach clinical PoM.
•Reduction in pTau217, GFAP, neurogranin, NfL, increase in Ab42/Ab40, slowing of decline in CDR-SB and ADAS-Cog score

People null for IFNAR1 are generally healthy, but can succeptible to live-attenuated virus & COVID. An anti-IFNAR1 antibody (non-brain penetrant) is FDA-approved (anifrolumab/Saphnelo) and hasdemonstrated to be safe for over 4 years. Live or live-attenuated vaccines should be avoided in patients receiving anti-IFNAR1 antibodies.

TCP_CHARACTERISTIC_VALUE: FIC bispecific to reduce B-cell survival and autoantibody production by neutralizing BAFF (TNFSF13B) and reduce inflammation, tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation, and tissue damage by blocking LIGHT (TNFSF14).

BAFFxLIGHT Ab/Nb molecule will bind to soluble BAFF preventing it from engaging with BAFF-R/BCMA/TACI and neutralizes both membrane and soluble LIGHT, preventing interaction with HVEM and LTβR. The expected effect is anti-inflammatory effect due to reduction autoantibodies, B/T cell as well as stromal cell activation.

Hidradenitis suppurativa, but the bispecific can be positioned in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus / Lupus Nephritis, Sjögren's syndrome, IBD, RA, and COPD/Asthma.

FIC, no direct competition. One approved monospecific for BAFF (Belimumab), another anti-BAFF (Tabalumab) failed in PHIII (SLE/RA). One monospecific for LIGHT (Quisovalimab) in PhII.
FiC

Autoimmune patients with high disease activity and multi-cellular immune contribution (B/T cells & TLS), anti-dsDNA positivity, e.g. HS, SLE, RA ​

HS non-responders to TNF and IL-17 inhibitors. Biomarker: TBD e.g. elevated B cell count, BAFF/LIGHT or CXCL13
IV and/or SC, ideally every 6-12 weeks
Reduces autoantibodies, inflammation and tissue damage, improves clinical response index i.e. HiSCR for HS, reduces flares and sustain durable effect.

Potential risk of immunosuppression and infection. However, based on the clinical trials of monospecific BAFF and LIGHT, it seems they are well tolerated with low-medium risk of infection and mild infusion reactions with low evidence of severe immunosuppression.
